survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses OECD PISA 2022 microdata to produce descriptive comparisons and correlational associations between student outcomes and contextual indices/items (e.g., digital education indicators and school disciplinary climate/safety). The methodology section describes bivariate and multivariate analyses and disaggregation by student characteristics, but it does not specify whether PISA sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the OECD’s internal analysis. For analysts working with PISA microdata, complex survey weights are typically required to obtain population-representative estimates and to account for the multistage sampling design (students nested in schools). Because the manuscript does not report the exact weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or replicate scheme, the safest practice is to apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided with the dataset when reproducing results.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD diagnostic review uses PISA 2022 as the primary quantitative evidence base to examine how digital education and school disciplinary climate/safety relate to students’ mathematics performance and learning conditions in Sweden. It combines student and school questionnaire indicators (e.g., indices of ICT availability and use; indices of disciplinary climate, bullying exposure, feeling safe, school safety risks, sense of belonging, student–teacher relationships, and teacher support in mathematics) with bivariate and multivariate correlational analyses, disaggregated by gender, socio-economic status (ESCS quartiles), immigrant background, and school location (rural/town/city). The report also presents trend evidence across PISA 2012–2022 for selected items/indices where comparability allows. It explicitly cautions that PISA is cross-sectional and that reported associations are not causal. Methodological details on PV handling and missing-data procedures are not provided in the excerpt, limiting exact reproducibility, but the substantive policy message is that supportive relationships coexist with classroom disruption and digital distraction risks, with inequities linked to socio-economic and immigrant background.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD diagnostic review rather than an empirical machine-learning study: it reports descriptive statistics and correlational associations from PISA 2022 (and some trend comparisons) and supplements them with stakeholder interviews and desk research. As a result, there is no ML model training/evaluation, no ML target-variable prediction pipeline, and no reported PV/missing-data handling workflow in the provided text. The absence of sample sizes and PV/missing-data documentation is consistent with a policy/diagnostic report format, but it constrains methodological transparency for replication.
